subject: Documentation for segmenting tracks with multiple areas of range-residency?

messages.author: 89513a910b665246
messages.subject: Documentation for segmenting tracks with multiple areas of range-residency?
parts:
Hi Chris,

I'm currently writing up home range estimation results for White-headed Vultures and am looking for a paper to cite...

A couple individuals exhibited range-residency in two separate protected areas. I decided that these areas were far enough apart, divided by habitat of lesser-quality, and utilized separately for long enough periods (to show range-residency on their own) that they warranted track segmentation.

Do you know of any published articles that I can cite as justification for segmentation as a part of the home range estimation workflow?

Thanks,

Teague

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Documentation for segmenting tracks with multiple areas of range-residency?
parts:
Hi Teague,

I'm working on a paper right now that discusses different methods for quantifying range residency. The very basic recommendation we have published in the MEE ctmm package paper regarding the variogram asymptote is about the most advanced thing that I have seen, unfortunately. You could cite that and show before and after variograms.

Ideally, this is a clustering problem, but autocorrelated cluster estimation that can also do model selection on the number of clusters does not yet exist to my knowledge.

Best,
Chris
